verification_report.summary: The complete supplement is correct under the accepted book inputs. All 12 proof items were checked sequentially, with seven reference/application checks. For n=1 the identity and a point give the required flag. For n>=2 the point blowup is smooth, connected and compact, and its exceptional projective space carries the complete smooth compact linear flag; the local construction matches [Complex Geometry, p.54](https://homepage.divms.uiowa.edu/~mftehrani/Complex%20Geometry.pdf#page=54). Hartogs applies to the holomorphic coefficient on a punctured trivializing ball, with no boundedness assumption; gluing and equality on the dense open set prove the section isomorphism for every m>=0 and compatibility with multiplication. See [Lebl, Theorem 4.3.1](https://math.okstate.edu/people/lebl/scv-f23/scv.pdf?1749427200010=#page=135). The actual accepted Gauduchon and intrinsic-count hypotheses all hold for the lifted graded algebra, without positivity or finite generation. Equal-degree section-ratio fields are identified by injective pullback, so d is their transcendence degree; e is the unchanged gcd of nonzero degrees. The denominator (eq)^d and translated lattice measure are exactly correct, and unchanged counts prove auxiliary-choice independence of V. For d=0, V=1 and supported degree pieces are eventually one-dimensional. Empty positive support is handled separately without assigning an undefined period. Vanishing outside eZ and finitely many initial degrees yield the asserted all-degree bounds. If d=n, independent original section ratios meet the accepted Moishezon theorem's hypotheses on X. The accepted Kahler-modification lemma gives Moishezon implies BMP, hence BMP failure implies non-Moishezon and the claimed lower-order growth. Arbitrary partial spaces inherit upper bounds by inclusion alone; no graded multiplier-ideal structure or multiplier-ideal pullback identity is asserted. Detailed checks are persisted in memory/auxiliary_blowup_flag_01. Book files were only read.
